doc.title: Billy McBride and Mary McBride ("Mack and Mack") Interview, 1959-07-01
doc.interviewee: Billy McBride and Mary McBride ("Mack and Mack")

title: The Dreamland and the Humphrey family
summary: Mary also worked at the Dreamland. They talk about Willie Humphrey and his father, nicknamed Little Belly, and sons Earl and Percy, whom the McBrides brought north.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: I did once go to the Dreamland. Richard M. Jones took me over to the Dreamland. I remember they had a big glass or mirror or something in the floor there too. She worked there. Did you work there too?
Yes, I worked there too. Well, and Willie Umfrey. Do you know him?
Is that the young Willie Umfrey? His father was named Willie too.
Yes, but the father was a father. We used to call him Little Belly. He was so fat, you know. They both play clarinet. Yes.
Well, they had one son that played trombone.
Yes, Earl. Earl Umfrey. We brought him here too.

And Percy, the drummer, now plays the trumpet. He's the leader of the Eureka Brass Band in New Orleans. He's still active. Both of them are active. Earl plays bass. He's over in Virginia. I've never met him.
We brought Umfrey here too. The old man.
The old man. We brought him here too.
